newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon lawyers protest against political pressure.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon lawyers protest against political pressure.

text.p: Lebanese lawyers stopped work for half an hour on Tuesday to protest against political interference in the judiciary, the head of the lawyer's union said.

"Lawyers all over Lebanon stopped work for half an hour at 10 o'clock to express their pain at what happened to the Constitutional Council, to protest against the powerful political interference in judicial matters and to put an end to it," Shakib Quortbawi told Reuters.
Judge Wajdi al-Mallat resigned from his position as president of the Constitutional Council last week.

He gave no reason for resigning but legal sources said the court was under pressure from top officials and politicians to restrict its decisions to three of the 19 cases in which it has been asked to overturn results of last year's parliamentary elections because of alleged intimidation and corruption.

"Unfortunately, Lebanon is not a state of law now. We will struggle to stop this situation in the future and to warn politicians not to go furthur in their interference in judicial affairs," Quortbawi said.
